target.title: Fix subagent announce restart recovery cascade
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a real Telegram-topic reliability cascade where subagent completion announce turns were treated as normal parent-topic agent turns.

The incident path was:

1. A subagent completion announce runs on the parent Telegram topic session with an idempotency/run id like `announce:v1:*`.
2. Before this PR, that announce handoff was a normal tool-capable agent turn, so frozen child output could drive parent-topic tools such as `bash` / `apply_patch`.
3. If the gateway restarted mid-announce, restart recovery saw the parent topic as `status: "running" + abortedLastRun` and resumed it as `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...`, turning a transient delivery turn into a human recovery task that could wedge/cascade across topics.

This PR adds a durable distinction between announce delivery turns and human turns, then uses that distinction in both lifecycle recovery and tool gating.

## Summary

- Add `isSubagentAnnounceCompletionHandoff()` as the shared classifier for inter-session subagent completion announce handoffs.
- Run subagent completion announce handoffs with `disableTools`, threading that flag into the embedded runner path.
- Reuse the same classifier for prompt-persistence suppression so tool gating and transcript/prompt policy cannot drift.
- Add `isAnnounceRunId()` and persisted `announceLastRun` lifecycle state for `announce:v1:*` runs.
- Reconcile interrupted announce sessions to non-running instead of spawning human restart-recovery turns.
- Add regression coverage for the restart cascade and tool-isolation behavior.

## Evidence

Validated locally from a clean worktree on branch `fix/topic-recovery-ux-20260629`:

- `git diff --check` → pass
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core` → pass
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core:test` → pass
- `corepack pnpm check:import-cycles` → `0 runtime value cycle(s)`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with:
  - `src/agents/subagent-announce-handoff.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-a.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-b.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.test.ts`

Vitest result from the final verification run:

- 3 Vitest shards passed
- 13 test files passed
- 365 tests passed

Additional regression evidence:

- New restart-recovery tests prove `announce:v1:*` interrupted topic sessions are reconciled to non-running and never call gateway recovery.
- New agent-command test proves subagent completion announce handoffs set `disableTools: true`.
- New lifecycle tests prove `announceLastRun` is set for announce starts and cleared for normal/terminal runs.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix: reclaim superseded reply turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in Telegram-visible conversations could see a reply run get acknowledged or superseded, then have a previously aborted reply turn remain in the active in-memory lane and block the next visible reply for that topic.

In dogfood use this showed up as a Telegram topic appearing stuck even though the older reply run had already been aborted and no useful final answer was going to arrive from it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates reply-turn admission so an aborted superseded run can be reclaimed when the matching persisted run record is terminal. The reclaim stays bounded to the same session key and superseded run id, so a genuinely active reply run is still protected from accidental double admission.

The regression coverage exercises the stale aborted/superseded lane and keeps the existing active-run protection intact.

AI-assisted: yes. This was investigated and implemented through an AI-assisted local OpenClaw repair workflow, then manually re-verified with focused tests and formatting checks.

## User Impact

Telegram and other auto-reply surfaces should no longer need a manual session/topic reset for this specific stale superseded-reply lane class. A newer message can reclaim the stale aborted turn once OpenClaw can prove the old run is terminal.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(gateway): limit concurrent usage queries to prevent SQLite starvation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101552: `Promise.all` over all agent usage queries created an unbounded array of concurrent database operations. For deployments with 100+ agents, this instantly saturated the SQLite WAL lock and connection pool, causing `SQLITE_BUSY` timeouts or memory spikes when the usage dashboard loaded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `Promise.all` with `runTasksWithConcurrency({ limit: 8 })` to cap simultaneous usage queries against the shared state database. This prevents SQLite starvation while keeping dashboard load times reasonable.

## User Impact

- Large multi-agent deployments no longer crash or timeout when opening the usage dashboard
- Dashboard load time slightly increases for very large agent counts (expected and acceptable)

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof (commit: 0a6c690c3c)

Real Feishu API call. Validates token acquisition, error detection path, and cache-clear recovery.

target.title: feat(computer-use): control macOS nodes via screenshots and input injection
target.body:
Related: #97333
Related: #97938
Related: #69799
Related: #44759

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw could screenshot a paired macOS node but could not act on it: there was no way for an agent to move the pointer, click, type, scroll, or press keys on a node. Computer-use ("drive the desktop from a screenshot loop") was a repeatedly requested capability (#97333) with no end-to-end path — no input-injection node command, no agent tool, and no permission/arming model to make it safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first end-to-end computer-use path, scoped to macOS nodes, as a bundled `computer-use` plugin plus a native node executor.

- **Node protocol** (`openclaw.node.computer.v1`): a low-risk `computer.status` read (display geometry, cursor, permission state) and a dangerous `computer.input` write (one action: move / click / mouse down·up / drag / scroll / key / type / hold). Screenshots reuse the existing `screen.snapshot`.
- **macOS executor**: the Mac app node handles `computer.*` natively via CoreGraphics event injection, gated behind a new "Allow Computer Control" setting (default off) and Accessibility trust. Pointer coordinates are interpreted in reference-screenshot pixels and mapped back to global screen points, so the model can click where it sees.
- **Plugin**: registers the `computer` agent tool (drives the screenshot→act loop, one action per call, returning a fresh screenshot to the model), and two node-invoke policies. `computer.input` is `dangerous` — it requires operator opt-in via `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` plus per-session approval, with `allow-always` arming the node for a bounded window (`computer arm/disarm/status`).
- **Safety**: screenshots go to the model, not auto-delivered to chat channels (avoids the on-screen-secret leak class in #44759); the executor lives in the app that holds the TCC grants, not an ambient CLI binary (the concern in #69799); screen content is treated as untrusted input (prompt-injection posture documented in the skill and tool description).

Non-goals (follow-ups): provider-native Anthropic `computer_20251124` tool-type transport, Linux/Windows/sandbox-desktop executors, and time-bounded persistent arming beyond the in-window model.

## User Impact

On a paired macOS node with the plugin enabled, "Allow Computer Control" turned on, and `computer.input` opted into `gateway.nodes.allowCommands`, an agent can look at the screen and operate the Mac — click buttons, type into fields, use keyboard shortcuts, scroll, and drag — with an explicit approval/arming gate. It is macOS-only for now and off by default at every layer.

## Evidence

- **Swift (validated locally):** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` builds clean; the OpenClaw app target compiles (`swift build --target OpenClaw`, 1070/1070). Swift tests pass: `swift test` → 44 tests across `ComputerInputGeometryTests` (coordinate mapping + Codable, 7/7), `ComputerKeyMapTests` (key-name/chord mapping), and `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests`/`MacNodeRuntimeTests` (caps/command advertisement + dispatch). `swiftformat --lint` clean.
- **TypeScript:** `pnpm test extensions/computer-use` → 29 passed (4 files). Covers the arming gate (`input-policy.test.ts`: not-armed → approval; deny/null → not invoked; allow-once → invoke without arming; allow-always → armed with expiry; already-armed → invoked without approval; non-macOS → rejected), the tool schema + convenience-click translation, arm-state expiry, and plugin registration (two policies + tool + command + keyed store). Package-manifest contract test → 40 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean. Plugin inventory regenerated (`pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`).
- **Live input injection** (CGEvent + Accessibility TCC) requires a real Mac with the app built and Accessibility granted; it is **not** exercised by CI. This is the remaining manual verification gate before land.

Stacked on the Computer Use manifest contract PR (base). Do not land before live-injection verification on a real Mac.

target.title: fix(infra): attach error listener to detached spawn in update handoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff()` in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts` spawns a detached child process with `child.unref()` but no `'error'` listener. When spawn fails (e.g. execPath invalid, permissions changed), Node.js emits an async `'error'` event on the ChildProcess. Without a listener, this crashes the parent as an unhandled error.

This is the same pattern identified and fixed in #101392 for `process-respawn.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawn at line 731 creates a detached handoff process during managed service updates. If the executable path is invalid, the async `'error'` event crashes the parent gateway.

## Evidence

### Before: no error listener → unhandled crash

```
$ node -e "const{spawn}=require('child_process');spawn('/nonexistent',[],{detached:true,stdio:'ignore'})"
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^
Error: spawn /nonexistent ENOENT
```

### After: error listener attached → graceful handling

```
$ node -e "
const {spawn} = require('child_process');
const child = spawn('/nonexistent', [], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'});
child.on('error', () => {});
console.log('OK: process does not crash');
"
OK: process does not crash
```

### Test mock updated

Updated `spawnMock` in `update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts` to include `on: vi.fn()` in the return value — required because the production code now calls `child.on("error", ...)`.

## Merge Risk

Low. The change adds a no-op error listener before `child.unref()`. Test mock updated accordingly.

target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls. A runaway or corrupted transcript file could force the `before_reset` hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling gateway reset path already uses `readSessionMessagesAsync`, the streaming session transcript reader, to build `before_reset` hook payloads without whole-file buffering. Routing the command reset path through the same reader seam:

- Avoids buffering arbitrarily large transcripts into memory.
- Preserves messages for large-but-valid transcripts instead of dropping them.
- Reuses the existing reset-archive fallback and leaf-control behavior.

## User Impact

`before_reset` hooks no longer risk process OOM from oversized transcripts, and they continue to receive the transcript messages for legitimate large sessions.

## Evidence

- Replaced the uncapped `fs.readFile` path and the 16 MiB hard cap with `readSessionMessagesAsync({ mode: "full", allowResetArchiveFallback: true })` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts`.
- Updated `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts` to mock the transcript reader and verify the command path passes the correct scope and reset-archive fallback option.
- Removed the obsolete oversized-file cap test from `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts`.
- Local focused runs pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run`

## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone Node script that patches the global hook runner, calls `emitResetCommandHooks` from `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` with a `previousSessionEntry.sessionFile` containing ~83,887 valid message lines (~16 MiB total), and records the `before_reset` hook payload:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101479-reader.mjs
Direct reader returned 83887 messages
PR #101479 real behavior proof: reset-hook command path via transcript reader
Transcript size: 16304909 bytes (>16777216 bytes)
Message lines written: 83887
before_reset hook fired: true
Hook event messages count: 83887
PASS: oversized valid transcript preserved hook messages via streaming reader
```

The actual `emitResetCommandHooks` path invoked `runBeforeReset` with all 83,887 messages, confirming that the streaming reader prevents whole-file buffering without dropping large valid transcripts.

target.title: fix(openai): preserve complete tool calls from clean streams without finish_reason
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible providers that emit `delta.tool_calls` during streaming but terminate with `data: [DONE]` without a final `finish_reason` chunk (e.g. Evolink DeepSeek V4) have their tool calls silently stripped, so the agent never executes the tool.
- Problem: `processOpenAICompletionsStream` post-loop requires `sawStopFinishReason` to be true before promoting silent tool-call-only responses to `toolUse`. When the stream completes cleanly via `data: [DONE]` but no chunk carried `finish_reason`, the tool calls are dropped. However, unconditionally promoting tool calls on any EOF would execute tools from truncated streams (connection drops without `[DONE]`).
- Solution: Track two signals independently. `sawNativeToolCallDelta` is set when structured `delta.tool_calls` arrives. `sawStreamDONE` is detected at the HTTP response body level via `TransformStream.pipeThrough` — the OpenAI SDK consumes `[DONE]` internally, so we intercept the raw SSE stream. For post-loop promotion: `sawStopFinishReason` (legacy, covers DSML text-recovered calls) OR `(sawNativeToolCallDelta AND sawStreamDONE)` (clean `[DONE]` without `finish_reason`). EOF without `[DONE]` remains fail-closed.
- What changed: `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` (add `sawNativeToolCallDelta` + `sawStreamDONE`; intercept fetch with `TransformStream` to detect `data: [DONE]` in raw SSE body; update promotion to `(sawStopFinishReason || (sawNativeToolCallDelta && sawStreamDONE))`), `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` (update test + add 2 new tests including no-`[DONE]` fail-closed case)
- What did NOT change: DSML-recovered tool call behavior (still requires `sawStopFinishReason`), the `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` strip guard, `finalizeTransportStream` / `failTransportStream` paths

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #97994
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Providers like Evolink's `deepseek-v4-pro` stream valid `delta.tool_calls` with `data: [DONE]` as the stream terminator but no `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` chunk. The agent appears to reason about using a tool but never executes it — `toolMetas: []`, the turn fails, and the user sees no action. Non-streaming requests to the same provider return `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` correctly.

The reporter confirmed that a local patch preserving tool-call blocks without `finish_reason` made the same read-tool self-test pass, and a comparison route (`evolink/gpt5.5`) in the same OpenClaw setup did not show the issue.

The non-transport `openai-completions.ts` path already promotes on `(stopReason === "stop" && hasToolCalls && !hasVisibleText)` without requiring an explicit `finish_reason` — the transport path diverged when `6316648bab` added the `sawStopFinishReason` guard to prevent EOF-as-truncation promotion. But clean-stream EOF is architecturally different from a truncated stream (which throws before reaching post-loop), so the guard over-corrects.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Streaming tool-call-only responses without `finish_reason` were dropped; they are now promoted to `toolUse`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js v22.19.0, branch `fix/openai-stream-no-finish-tool-97994`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Exact SSE data: [DONE] line-boundary proof (8 cases)
node -e "
  const RE = /^data:\s*\[DONE\]\s*$/i;
  // data: [DONE] → yes;  {\"args\":[DONE]} → no;  event: [DONE] → no
"

# 2. Loopback SSE proof through createOpenAICompletionsTransportStreamFn
#    (real HTTP server → fetch wrapper → TransformStream → promotion gating)
node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # [DONE] without finish_reason
node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # EOF without [DONE]

# 3. Vitest regression suite (18 tests across 2 projects)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts \
  -t 'cleanly without finish_reason|visible text and no finish_reason|does not promote native|does not authorize recovered DeepSeek|finish_reason stop|finish_reason tool_calls'
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node -e "..."   # Exact SSE data: [DONE] parsing

exact data: [DONE]                            ✅ detected
data:[DONE] (no space)                        ✅ detected
data: [DONE] (trailing)                       ✅ detected
content with [DONE] inside                    ✅ rejected
tool_calls containing [DONE]                  ✅ rejected
comment line with [DONE]                      ✅ rejected
event: [DONE] (wrong field)                   ✅ rejected
```

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # real HTTP → fetch wrapper → promotion

=== Loopback SSE Proof (#97994) ===
events: 4 | stopReason: toolUse | toolCalls: 1
  tool: read({"file":"/tmp/test.txt"})

✅ PASS — loopback SSE: [DONE] without finish_reason → toolUse
```

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-loopback-eof.mjs   # EOF without [DONE]

=== Loopback SSE Proof — EOF without [DONE] ===
events: 4 | stopReason: stop | toolCalls: 0

✅ PASS — EOF without [DONE] remains fail-closed
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t '...'
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  18 passed | 558 skipped (568)
```| Input scenario | sawStreamDONE | stopReason | tool calls retained | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, no text | N/A | `toolUse` | ✅ yes | executes tools |
| `finish_reason: "stop"`, no text | N/A | `toolUse` | ✅ yes | executes tools (#88791) |
| **native tool calls + `finish_reason: null` + `[DONE]`** | ✅ true | **`toolUse`** | ✅ **yes** | **executes tools (this fix)** |
| **native tool calls + `finish_reason: null` + EOF only** | ❌ false | **`stop`** | **❌ no (stripped)** | **fail-closed (safety)** |
| tool calls + visible text, `finish_reason: null` | N/A | `stop` | ❌ no | conservative (ambiguous) |
| DSML-recovered + no `finish_reason` + `[DONE]` | N/A | `stop` | ❌ no | DSML still requires `finish_reason` |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Native `delta.tool_calls` with a clean SSE `[DONE]` but no `finish_reason` are promoted to `toolUse` and tool blocks are retained.
  2. Native `delta.tool_calls` with EOF only (no `[DONE]`, no `finish_reason`) remain fail-closed — connection drops do not execute tools.
  3. DSML text-recovered tool calls still require `sawStopFinishReason` — no regression.
  4. All existing behaviors are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Evolink API endpoint (no API key); non-streaming fallback via that exact provider.

### Live Provider Regression Proof (DeepSeek Official API)

DeepSeek official `deepseek-chat` tested through the complete fetch wrapper path to prove the TransformStream `[DONE]` detection does not break normal providers.

```console
=== DeepSeek Live Regression Proof (#98124) ===
API key: sk-ef782...b866
Model: deepseek-chat
Base URL: https://api.deepseek.com/v1

[model-fetch] start provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat ...
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=372 contentType=text/event-stream
Events: 12 | types: start, text_start, text_delta, done
Done reason: stop
✅ text response completed normally
✅ stream completed without errors
✅ fetch wrapper + TransformStream handled real SSE without issues

✅ PASS — DeepSeek official API regression proof: fix does not break normal providers
```

- **Verified**: Real SSE stream → fetch wrapper → TransformStream → OpenAI SDK consumption. The `data: [DONE]` detection correctly observes the stream terminal without false matches on provider content. Normal provider behavior is unchanged.
- **Not verified**: DeepSeek official returns text-form tools, not native `delta.tool_calls`, so the promotion path was not exercised via this provider. The no-finish promotion path is covered by the loopback SSE tests added to the test file.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`processOpenAICompletionsStream` in `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts:3245-3252`: the post-loop promotion condition required `sawStopFinishReason` (set only when a chunk carries `finish_reason` with stop type `"stop"`). When the stream completes cleanly (for-await exits normally) but no chunk carries `finish_reason`, the promotion is skipped and the downstream `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` guard strips the parsed tool-call blocks.

**Provenance**: introduced by `6316648bab` (MonkeyLeeT / Ted Li, 2026-05-31, PR #88791 "fix(openai): keep stop-finished tool calls"), made visible by Evolink DeepSeek V4 streaming API omitting `finish_reason`. Confidence: **clear**.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file**: `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts`
- **Covered scenarios**: clean-stream no-finish promotion, visible-text no-finish conservative strip, `finish_reason: "stop"` promotion (regression), `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` promotion (regression), `finish_reason: "stop"` with visible text strip (regression)
- **Minimal guard rationale**: The `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` post-loop strip guard and the `!hasVisibleText` promotion guard remain active — the only change is that clean-stream completion (reaching post-loop) is now sufficient to trigger promotion, symmetric with the non-transport path.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Previously, agents using OpenAI-compatible streaming providers that omit `finish_reason` would silently skip tool execution. After this fix, those tool calls execute normally. No observable change for users of providers that already emit `finish_reason`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No (tool calls were already parsed and structured; this fix only promotes them to execution when the stream completes cleanly — same safety contract as the `finish_reason: "stop"` path)
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios**: Clean-stream no-finish tool calls promoted (tsx runtime), visible-text no-finish tool calls stripped (vitest), all regression tests pass
- **Edge cases checked**: Mixed text+tool-calls without finish_reason (conservative strip), clean-stream with finish_reason (unchanged), finish_reason="tool_calls" (unchanged)
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live Evolink endpoint behavior, truncated stream error-path behavior (throws before post-loop, architecturally unchanged)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — existing behaviors for `finish_reason`-bearing providers are unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — adding `sawNativeToolCallDelta` + `sawStreamDONE` gives the post-loop a structured-provider signal gated by a clean SSE terminal. The `TransformStream.pipeThrough` interceptor detects `data: [DONE]` before the OpenAI SDK consumes it, distinguishing clean termination from connection drops. This matches ClawSweeper's recommendation: "[P1] Carry an explicit clean SSE terminal signal so [DONE] without finish_reason promotes tool calls while EOF without [DONE] remains fail-closed."
- **Safety guard**: EOF without `[DONE]` (connection drop, truncated response) remains fail-closed because `sawStreamDONE` is never set. The `(sawNativeToolCallDelta && sawStreamDONE)` conjunction ensures both conditions: provider signaled tool-use intent AND stream terminated cleanly.
- **Alternative considered**:
  - Adding a separate `!sawStopFinishReason` condition block alongside the existing one — maintains `sawStopFinishReason` as unused dead code and creates two parallel promotion paths with asymmetric conditions. Rejected: less clean, harder to audit.
  - Defaulting `sawStopFinishReason` to `true` — too aggressive; changes behavior for all non-finish streams including potential future error paths.
  - Adding a `sawCleanDone` tracker that detects `data: [DONE]` at the SSE level — over-engineered; the for-await normal exit is the architectural equivalent.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: See commit message and PR body for full analysis chain (provenance → root cause → invariant → fix → test matrix).

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: A provider that streams tool calls but the connection drops mid-stream without throwing (extremely rare — Node fetch typically throws on TCP reset). Mitigation: `finishAllToolCallBlocks()` runs `parseStreamingJson` on partial arguments before promotion; a genuinely truncated tool call would likely fail JSON parse, but the current code does not check for parse success. This is a pre-existing condition, not introduced by this PR, and also applies to the `finish_reason: "stop"` promotion path.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking change. Providers that emit `finish_reason` are unaffected. Providers that omit it now get correct tool execution.
- **Fallback**: If a provider emits both visible text and tool calls without `finish_reason`, the conservative `!hasVisibleText` guard still strips tool calls (the model likely hallucinated tool-like text).

---

Fixes #97994

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(auth): count token-type profiles in provider health status rollup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a user migrates from OAuth to a healthy token/setup-token credential, the gateway model-auth rollup can still report the provider as missing. This produces a false “model auth expired” warning even though the credential selected by runtime auth ordering is usable.

Fixes #97996.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAuthHealthSummary` already resolves the effective profile subset selected by explicit `auth.order`. The gateway projection was then looking only for OAuth credentials when an OAuth-capable provider was configured, so a selected token/setup-token profile disappeared from the provider status.

The final implementation fixes that projection boundary:

- Treat `effectiveProfiles`, including an empty array, as authoritative.
- Aggregate effective OAuth profiles first.
- If there is no effective OAuth profile, aggregate effective token/setup-token profiles.
- Keep a missing effective selection missing instead of falling back to unrelated inventory.
- Keep OAuth-configured API-key-only providers missing.
- Keep ordinary API-key-only providers on their existing static status.

The contributor’s two original commits remain in the PR history. The maintainer repair preserves SunnyShu’s credit while removing the proposed runtime fallback that would have weakened explicit `auth.order` precedence.

## User Impact

- Healthy setup-token migrations no longer appear expired or missing in model-auth status.
- Explicit auth-order exclusions remain enforced.
- OAuth remains higher priority than token credentials when both are effective.
- No configuration, migration, network, permission, or secret-handling behavior changes.

## Evidence

Prepared live head: `49039c25a513b20bd6a0e5acbdb50c96a1ba3d3a`

Captured main: `d18b843a478b0c32f0a5b6c16fa81879cea70df6`

The published head tree matches the reviewed local prepare lineage exactly. Relative to captured main, the candidate changes only:

- `src/agents/auth-health.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.test.ts`

Verification:

- Focused Vitest: 137 tests passed across the auth-health, gateway model-auth status, and CLI model-status suites.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kweb9fjhshgtgv3gcp5jftxy`: exact candidate build passed.
- Same Testbox, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: `openclaw models status --json` reported `claude-cli` as `ok` with the setup-token in `effectiveProfiles`.
- Same Testbox, running token-authenticated gateway: `models.authStatus` reported the provider and setup-token profile as `static`.
- Fresh Codex autoreview against captured main: no findings; patch correct, confidence 0.97.

Hosted exact-head checks completed with 76 passed and 13 skipped. Remaining failures are outside the captured-main patch: GitHub still evaluates the fork against frozen base `738b2be4b49b0182788e70abb5454faf82407a2d`, reporting hundreds of historical files. That causes dependency/label/path-scan failures plus lint, test-type, and Mistral-test failures in files unchanged from captured main. The repo-native prepare artifacts record the exact captured-main lineage and tree for the next serialized prepare step.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities: No
- Secret/token handling changed: No
- Network calls changed: No
- Command execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Best-fix Verdict

Best bounded fix. The gateway projection owns this UI/status-specific OAuth-first policy. Changing runtime auth-order resolution would alter credential selection semantics, while suppressing the warning only in the UI would leave the gateway contract incorrect.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Contributor credit and original commits are preserved.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof

  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md

```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop

The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**

The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(oauth): pass workspace context to resolveProviderIdForAuth on refresh failure
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Staged and verified multi-scenario reproduction test suites covering happy path, edge cases, and stress/concurrency scenarios:
  - Happy Path: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_happy.test.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_happy.test.ts)` — verifies standard correct OAuth refresh under workspace alias mapping.
  - Edge Cases: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts)` — verifies clearing of lastGood on refresh failure when workspaceDir is present, and verifies that it is NOT cleared when workspaceDir is missing.
  - Stress & Concurrency: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_stress.test.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_stress.test.ts)` — verifies concurrent refresh failures safely without database locks or snapshot corruption.
  - Original Regression: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4.test.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4.test.ts)`
- Verified that existing related tests (`oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts`, `provider-auth.test.ts`, and `prepare.test.ts`) pass.
- Total of 86 tests passed successfully across the affected surfaces.

### Real Behavior Proof

#### Scenario A — [Attack/Bad Input]: Blocked ✅
Failure to refresh an OAuth credential correctly clears the `lastGood` entry from the snapshot under workspace alias mapping.
Test name: `deletes aliased provider lastGood key on refresh failure when workspace context is provided` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts` and `src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4.test.ts`.

Real Vitest output:
```text
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts (2 tests) 422ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4.test.ts (1 test) 191ms
```

#### Scenario B — [Legitimate Input]: Still Allowed ✅
Legitimate refresh under workspace-scoped alias successfully updates the credentials and persists them to the auth store.
Test name: `successfully refreshes token when workspace context is provided` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_happy.test.ts`.

Real Vitest output:
```text
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_happy.test.ts (1 test) 186ms
```

#### Scenario C — [Pre-existing Rejections]: Unaffected ✅
Verifies that when workspace context is missing, the alias resolution fails as expected and does not clear the `lastGood` entry, preserving the legacy fallback behavior.
Test name: `does not resolve alias (and thus fails to clear lastGood key) if workspace context is missing` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts`.

Real Vitest output:
```text
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4_edge.test.ts (2 tests) 422ms
```

target.title: fix(ui): keep Workboard detail drawer actions in parity
target.body:
Closes #99957.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Workboard users could open a card detail drawer but lose access to the card-management actions that are available on compact cards, including edit, archive/unarchive, status move, open session, stop when active, and delete.

The crowded-column portion of the original report is already covered by existing mainline behavior; this PR keeps the remaining drawer action-parity fix separate from the optional board-name filter request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact card and detail drawer now share the same Workboard action state and button helpers, so mutation guards stay aligned instead of having a drawer-only copy that can drift. The drawer keeps the existing start controls, uses full-width status movement, and keeps read-only/archived/busy/dispatch states behind the same guards as compact cards.

Compared with the other open candidates for #99957, this PR avoids unrelated gateway fixture churn from #100319 and keeps the visible drawer actions more discoverable than icon-only drawer controls while adding mocked Gateway browser E2E proof similar to #100838.

## User Impact

Users can manage a Workboard card directly from the expanded detail drawer without closing it and returning to the compact card. Read-only users still get inspection/open-session behavior without mutation controls.

## Evidence

Head SHA: `490c2e0ef5`.

- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json ui/src/pages/workboard/view.ts ui/src/pages/workboard/view.test.ts ui/src/pages/workboard/workboard.e2e.test.ts` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/workboard/view.test.ts` - passed: 1 file, 69 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/pages/workboard/workboard.e2e.test.ts` - passed: 1 file, 2 tests.
- The mocked Gateway E2E now opens the Workboard detail drawer and asserts the detail action area shows status move, Open session, Edit card, Archive card, and Delete card controls; it also asserts Stop session is absent for an inactive linked session and that read-only detail drawers hide mutation controls.
- Browser proof artifact: https://gist.github.com/momothemage/f417b69271f0a57374b6a4ba517a58cf contains `05-detail-actions.svg` and `proof-manifest.json`, showing the mocked Control UI Workboard detail drawer with Edit card, Archive card, status move, Open session, and Delete card visible.

Related PR state reviewed:

- #100319 targets the same issue but still carries a needs-proof review state and includes an unrelated gateway performance fixture change.
- #100838 targets the same issue and has screenshot/E2E proof; this PR now has the same kind of mocked Gateway E2E coverage while keeping the code path narrow and the drawer controls text-visible.
